summary: Assign environment lighting, roughness prefiltering, direct lights and shadow maps separate jobs so a Blender HDR look becomes a controlled Three.js lighting rig rather than an unexplained brightness match.
objective: Reflective materials keep readable roughness variation, a named direct light owns the grounding shadow, and changing environment intensity does not masquerade as changing shadow-map behavior.
intent_signals: HDRI lights object but there is no ground shadow
match Blender world lighting in Three.js
example_prompts: Bring this Blender HDR studio setup into Three.js with a stable grounding shadow.
Separate the environment reflection from the sun shadow in this product viewer.
negative_signals: assume the environment image casts shadow maps
add many shadow lights without purpose
pixel-match unrelated path tracing and raster lighting
not_for: Claiming an HDR image reproduces measured illumination without calibration.
Treating a direct-light raster setup as equivalent to Blender path tracing.

principles: Give the environment three explicit responsibilities: broad illumination, reflected surroundings and backdrop if desired. Backdrop visibility remains a presentation choice.
Prefilter the environment for the PBR material model so rough surfaces can sample wider reflection lobes. PMREM is a runtime representation choice, not a new light source.
Assign hard or directional grounding shadows to named direct lights and shadow maps, or to a declared baked/fake shadow. An HDR environment alone does not define that shadow ownership in Three.js.

A Blender world/render match is conditional on world rotation, intensity, direct lights, exposure, view transform, material model and bounce behavior. Record differences rather than compensating all of them with one intensity slider.
implementation: Export material and geometry separately from the lighting contract. Record the Blender world image, rotation, strength, direct lights, render engine, exposure and view transform as reference settings.

In Three.js, load the HDR environment with its linear high-dynamic-range color role and assign the renderer-appropriate prefiltered result to scene.environment. Keep scene.background independent when the backdrop should differ.

Add only the direct lights whose jobs are named. For a grounding sun/key shadow, enable renderer shadow maps, light castShadow, object castShadow and receiver receiveShadow, then fit the shadow camera to the relevant region.

Tune environment intensity for material readability and direct-light intensity for its named illumination/shadow contrast while holding exposure fixed. Use a neutral roughness ladder and a grounded object as diagnostics.
Record Three.js revision and renderer/backend because environment preprocessing and shadow features differ across paths and releases.
observable_checks: A roughness ladder reflects progressively broader environment features rather than the same sharp image at every step.
Disabling the named shadow-casting direct light removes its grounding shadow while leaving environment reflections present.
Rotating the environment moves reflected features; the direct light's shadow direction stays fixed unless that light is also rotated.
The shadow remains inside its fitted camera through the intended interaction range and does not disappear at the near/far boundaries.

creative_affordances: Use an invented gradient environment or studio-card scene instead of a photographic HDR when it better shapes the object.
A blob shadow or baked contact patch can replace a shadow map in a stylized scene when its ownership and limits are clear.
known_limits: This profile does not reproduce global illumination, caustics or all bounce lighting from Blender.
Environment-map and shadow APIs vary by Three.js renderer and release; inspect the selected path.
Authored reusable guidance; no HDR was loaded and no shadow was rendered for this record.

claims.statement: Three.js PMREMGenerator produces a prefiltered mipmapped radiance environment map whose filtered levels are selected for material roughness and whose prefiltering targets the GGX BRDF used for physically based image-based lighting.
claims.scope: Current Three.js PMREMGenerator behavior; it does not guarantee agreement with Blender's sampling, world shader or render engine.

claims.statement: Three.js documents shadow maps as separate renders from each shadow-casting light and requires renderer shadow maps plus per-light and per-mesh cast/receive settings; environment assignment is documented separately as PBR environment lighting.
claims.scope: Current Three.js shadow-map and scene-environment model; baked or custom shadow methods are outside this claim.
